author: Singular Research
title: Will Earnings Normalize Soon?
text:
Singular Research Director's Letter, April 2018
The U.S equity markets are not getting much credit from the tax cuts yet this year. Earnings will be up a record 21%, the best showing in many years. We will focus on revenue growth in the quarter ahead, as well as on estimates and guidance. Investors are trying to figure out what the real rate of earnings growth is at this point, counterbalanced against rising interest rates. It looks like the peak for operating margins is in as real growth is found in lower margins vs. financially engineered EPS growth.
The FANG - Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ), and Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) - stocks continue to beat earnings growth estimates. In particular, Facebook and Google rank among the top spending corporations with lobbyists in D.C. As forward-thinking corporate planners, they are ardently paving the way for future growth, fighting off the "break up the beasts" sentiments. This success is evidenced by the recent testimony by Facebook's Mark Zuckerberg in front of Congress. Where is the outrage? Where are the new proposals to protect our privacy? Facebook will still be allowed to self-regulate. What would you pay for 20% to 25% earnings growth for the next five to 10 years, with virtually no competition? Certainly more than the 20% to 30% premium the FANG stocks are trading to the market right now.
Meanwhile, Q2 earnings are to the upside with Q3 expected to be up over 20% as well. Valuations are not crazy at a slight premium to the five-year average and historical average. Interest rates are still below average. But the market seems fairly valued and higher earnings are needed to propel the market higher from this level. Is the Fed neutral, based on money supply growth and GDP growth? This seems to be the case. Should we worry that the spread between the two-year and 10-year government bond is narrowing down to 40 basis points? Usually this is a strong indicator that a recession is on the horizon. Meanwhile, the leading economic indicators continue to edge higher, a very good sign for the economy and the market.
In summary, it might be good to hold in May and June and go play. It looks as if the market is going to have to grind it out until it has evidence that there is solid earnings growth ahead into early 2019. Also, the midterm elections in November will start to become an overhang and create another potential negative for the market. Another key question is: Will the market normalize and take the benefit of the tax cuts and reinvest into the real economy? Or will it continue to engage in financial engineering via share buybacks and mergers and acquisitions? Don't get faked out, stay long.
April's top performers combined were an eclectic bunch, with varied influences likely contributing to outperformance. General Finance ( GFN ) posted a strong Q1 and raised estimates slightly. EVIO ( OTCQB:EVIO ) was a new initiation with favorable news on its growth plans, and Huttig Building Products ( HBP ) bounced back from an extreme oversold condition.
The worst performers list was led by LSI Industries ( LYTS ), hit with a surprise resignation of its CEO. That was followed by NMI Holdings ( NMIH ), suffering from some surprising price cuts by a competitor that spooked the market on the outlook for future margins. That was closely followed to the downside by Salem Media( SALM ), as investors continued to abandon a sector perceived to be another casualty of technological disruption and an aging audience.
We are excited to announce new coverage on EVIO. It is a leading provider of quality control testing, consulting and advisory services to the cannabis industry. We believe it has aggressive growth potential as an emerging leader in this nascent industry. The company owns nine laboratories serving five states in the U.S. - California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Oregon, and Florida.
At Singular Research, we continue to seek out investment ideas that have minimal to no Wall Street coverage to add alpha for our active institutional following. We thank you for your support of independent equity research.
